messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: Deploy pipeline failed for release/hotfix-2026.03.15 - GH Actions runners reporting registry 5xx when pushing artifacts (ghcr/npm). Auto-page on-call.

maria: i'm on it, paging raj. seeing `500` and `503` on ghcr.io and npm publish jobs. full logs attached in job 4821.

raj: looking. can you paste the first failing step log?

maria: job snippet:
```
Uploading artifact to GHCR...
response status: 503 Service Unavailable
retrying (1/3)...
Uploading package to npm...
npm ERR! code E500
npm ERR! 503 Service Unavailable - GET https://registry.npmjs.org/@our-org/package - from npm publish
```

olivia: this is blocking the hotfix merge -> can't roll forward. Are we able to use a different runner or mirror the registry?

sam: quick note: CI uses GH Actions with AWS-hosted runners and we push docker images to ghcr and npm to npmjs. If GH tokens are being rate-limited that could explain failures.

raj: checking GitHub status API now.

github-status-bot: GitHub Status: Partial Outage affecting Actions and the Package Registry - https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/abcd1234 (updated 2m ago)

maria: ok that's consistent. Any ETA from GitHub?

raj: status page says engineers investigating, no ETA. If Actions runners are flaky, alternatives: 1) run self-hosted runner in our VPC (fastest), 2) push artifacts to an internal S3 mirror and trigger deploy manually, 3) delay release.

olivia: option 1 is risky for a hotfix (not prepared). option 2 sounds doable - can we publish to internal artifact-store and update deploy to pull from there?

sam: yes we have an internal npm mirror (verdaccio) behind auth, and an S3-backed docker registry used for staging. We can publish there, but release engineering needs to flip the image source in k8s deploy or use a short-lived tagging flow.

jess: CS update: a handful of enterprise customers reported degraded responses in their apps (error 503s) around the same window. We likely have partial customer impact if deploys aren't going out but more immediate is integration failures for onboarding flows that rely on GitHub webhooks.

maria: i'm going to try a manual publish to our internal mirror from my laptop with `npm publish --registry https://verdaccio.internal/` and `docker push s3-registry.internal/our-app:hotfix-2026-03-15`. I'll report back.

raj: before that, quick check - are tokens healthy? GitHub apps auth is fine for API calls but Actions service uses different token paths. Logs show `403` and `429` intermittently earlier, now mostly `5xx` from package endpoints. Could be partial upstream outage at package registry layer.

maria: manual npm publish to verdaccio succeeded. docker push to internal registry also succeeded.

olivia: great. what's the safest way to get these artifacts deployed to production without changing a ton?

sam: we can create a one-off ImagePull override in k8s for the hotfix rollout: `kubectl set image deployment/web web=registry.internal/our-app:hotfix-2026-03-15` and create a short-lived feature flag to route small percentage. No need to touch main CI.

raj: runbook check: ensure we 1) sign artifacts appropriately, 2) record provenance in the release note, 3) revoke or rotate any tokens if we suspect auth issues later.

maria: doing the rollout now. running: 
```sh
kubectl set image deployment/web web=registry.internal/our-app:hotfix-2026-03-15 -n prod
kubectl rollout status deployment/web -n prod
```

deploy-bot: started rollout for deployment/web by maria at 1948510203

olivia: monitoring dashboards for error rates and latency.

raj: monitoring GH status updates. also opened support ticket with GitHub (ticket# 98765) including job ids and timestamps. Requested priority escalation given we have blocked hotfixes.

github-status-bot: GitHub Status: Engineers investigating package registry outages; updates expected every 15 minutes.

sam: quick question for security - kai, any concern with using internal mirror for production artifacts for hotfix?

kai: acceptable for emergency hotfixes. Make sure we sign and store checksum in secure release notes. We'll do a quick post-deploy audit.

maria: rollout finished: `deployment \"web\" successfully rolled out` and health checks green. Verified smoke tests passing.

jess: telling affected customers we deployed mitigations and will follow up. No broad customer-facing incident postmortem yet.

olivia: thanks team. next steps: 1) document the emergency mirror flow in runbook, 2) follow up with GH support and capture root cause, 3) rotate tokens if needed, 4) add detection on our CI for package registry 5xx to auto-fallback to mirror.

raj: logging: ticket#98765 and incident record created under INC-2026-0315-GHA. Will link GH status updates and timeline.

maria: adding notes to the incident doc and marking on-call handoff to raj for overnight follow-up. 

raj: taking handoff. will watch status and coordinate with GH.

olivia: great work, team :thumbsup:
